summary.title: Privacy Enhancing Technologies: An Introduction for Technologists
summary.one_liner: You learn the three production-ready privacy enhancing technologies (differential privacy, distributed/federated analysis and learning, and encrypted computation) and where each fits in data systems.
keywords: protect user data in machine learning
takeaways: Differential privacy measures an individual's privacy loss and bounds it by adding calibrated noise based on query sensitivity.
Federated learning keeps raw data on devices or in original storage and shares only model updates or aggregate results, supporting data minimization.
Encrypted computation (homomorphic encryption and MPC) lets parties compute on encrypted or secret-shared data and reveal only the final result.
Private set intersection lets parties find shared identifiers without exchanging the identifiers in plaintext.
These tools involve privacy vs utility tradeoffs and are available as libraries such as Tumult Analytics, OpenMined, PipelineDP, Opacus and Flower.
summary.summary: Martin Fowler's article, adapted from Katharine Jarmul's O'Reilly book Practical Data Privacy, introduces Privacy Enhancing Technologies that are considered production-ready and rigorous. It explains differential privacy with a US Census example and the concepts of sensitivity and noise mechanisms, then covers distributed and federated analysis and learning as a way to practice data minimization. It closes with encrypted computation, contrasting homomorphic encryption and secure multi-party computation, and gives use cases such as private set intersection. The article is conceptual, points to libraries and further resources, and does not include implementation code.
